title: Sub-7B open-weight reasoning models clear verified AIME-80 by Q1 2027
body: WeiboAI's VibeThinker-3B, a dense 3-billion-parameter MIT-licensed model built on Qwen2.5-3B, claims roughly 76 on AIME (into the 80s with test-time scaling) and about 80 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6 using its Spectrum-to-Signal post-training pipeline, but those figures are self-reported and await reproduction. Set against the wider open-weight efficiency wave now landing weekly — GLM-5.2's fully-open MIT weights, vLLM v0.23.0 and SGLang v0.5.13 serving releases, and MosaicQuant 4-bit quantization — the trajectory points one way: post-training recipes, not parameter count, are closing the small-model reasoning gap. The prediction is that at least one open-weight model at or under 7 billion parameters will post an AIME score in the 80s that is corroborated on an independent third-party leaderboard or reproduction (not just the releasing team's own card), confirming that frontier verifiable-reasoning quality has moved into a size class that runs on a single consumer GPU or a high-end laptop.

reasoning.because: VibeThinker-3B (MIT, 3B) claims ~76 AIME rising into the 80s, on a model that runs almost anywhere
reasoning.given: Open-weight post-training and serving recipes (GLM-5.2, vLLM, SGLang, MosaicQuant) compound weekly
reasoning.so_that: An independent leaderboard or reproduction corroborates an 80s-AIME score from a model at or under 7B parameters
reasoning.landing: by Q1 2027; a third-party leaderboard verifies a sub-7B model at AIME-80
reasoning.plain_language: Tiny free AI models that fit on one computer are getting good enough at hard math that outsiders will confirm the scores.

summary: VibeThinker-3B claims AIME scores in the 80s for a 3B MIT-licensed model, but the numbers are self-reported. Amid a weekly cadence of open-weight and inference-efficiency releases, expect an independent leaderboard or reproduction to corroborate an 80s-AIME score from a sub-7B model by Q1 2027.
